originalTitle: Saudi Arabia crude oil exports hit highest level since Iran war began despite pipeline outage
summary: Saudi exports are rising despite escalating attacks on its infrastructure from Iran-backed militants in Yemen and Iraq.
content:
Saudi Arabia's crude oil exports have surged this month despite a sharp escalation in fighting with Iran-backed militants, according to data from the trade intelligence firm Kpler.

Riyadh is exporting 6 million barrels per day in September, the highest level since the Iran war began about seven months ago. The kingdom's crude shipments have recovered to the monthly average of 2025.

The Saudis have managed to ramp up exports even after they closed the critical East-West oil pipeline this month due to damage it sustained in a drone attack launched from Iraq. Shipments in September have surged nearly 80% over the 3.4 million bpd of crude exported in August.

The pipeline has acted as a crucial relief valve for the oil market during the Iran war. It allowed the Saudis to bypass the Strait of Hormuz as Iran attacked tankers transiting those waters. Riyadh shifted exports from its oil-producing regions in the east through the pipeline to the Red Sea terminal of Yanbu.

Brent crude oil jumped to nearly $110 per barrel after the pipeline shut, but prices have pulled back as investor confidence grows that the outage has been less disruptive than originally feared.

The Saudis have redirected crude oil exports back through Hormuz as the U.S. military has carved out a shipping lane along Oman's coast. The other Gulf states have relied on this route for months now, though the journey remains dangerous as Iran continues to attack tankers transiting the strait.

"The ramp-up from the Mideast Gulf is a consequence of the pipeline outage, but it likely also signals a greater confidence in using the Strait of Hormuz given rising traffic," said Matt Smith, director of commodity research at Kpler.

Oil exports through Hormuz reached a seven-day average of 13.2 million bpd on Wednesday, compared with around 17 million bpd before the Iran war disrupted traffic, according Kpler data.

Industry sources told Reuters that the East-West pipeline restarted at low volumes earlier this week and is now ramping up. Saudi Arabia has not publicly confirmed that the pipeline has restarted.

But Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser told the Japanese newspaper Nikkei on Thursday that "temporary interruptions" to oil infrastructure last "usually for days, not weeks or months ... on every occasion." Nasser declined to give a specific update on the pipeline.
chineseTitle: 尽管管道中断，沙特阿拉伯原油出口仍创伊朗战争爆发以来最高水平
chineseSummary: 尽管伊朗支持的也门和伊拉克武装分子对其基础设施的攻击不断升级，但沙特的出口仍在增长。
chineseContent:
贸易情报公司 Kpler 的数据显示，尽管与伊朗支持的武装分子的战斗急剧升级，但本月沙特阿拉伯的原油出口仍大幅增长。

利雅得9月份每天出口600万桶，这是自大约七个月前伊朗战争开始以来的最高水平。沙特原油出货量已恢复至2025年的月平均水平。

尽管沙特本月关闭了重要的东西方石油管道，但由于伊拉克无人机袭击造成的损坏，沙特仍设法增加了出口。 9 月份的原油出口量较 8 月份的 340 万桶/日激增近 80%。

该管道在伊朗战争期间充当了石油市场的重要安全阀。当伊朗袭击经过霍尔木兹海峡的油轮时，它允许沙特绕过霍尔木兹海峡。利雅得通过管道将东部产油区的出口转移到红海延布码头。

管道关闭后，布伦特原油价格跃升至每桶近 110 美元，但随着投资者信心增强，认为停电造成的破坏性没有最初担心的那么严重，价格已回落。

随着美国军方沿着阿曼海岸开辟一条航道，沙特已将原油出口重新调整为通过霍尔木兹。其他海湾国家几个月来一直依赖这条航线，尽管由于伊朗继续袭击通过该海峡的油轮，这条航线仍然很危险。

Kpler 大宗商品研究主管马特·史密斯 (Matt Smith) 表示：“中东海湾的流量增加是管道中断的结果，但这也可能表明，鉴于交通量不断增加，人们对使用霍尔木兹海峡的信心更大。”

Kpler 数据显示，周三，通过霍尔木兹的石油出口量达到 7 天平均每日 1,320 万桶，而伊朗战争中断交通之前约为每日 1,700 万桶。

业内消息人士告诉路透社，东西方管道本周早些时候以少量重启，目前正在增加。沙特阿拉伯尚未公开证实该管道已重新启动。

但沙特阿美公司首席执行官阿明·纳赛尔周四对日本《日经新闻》表示，石油基础设施的“暂时中断”“通常会持续数天，而不是数周或数月……每次都会”。纳赛尔拒绝透露有关管道的具体更新信息。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
